definitions.gloss: from beginning to end, the whole story
definitions.explanation: The entire process or sequence of events.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{始終|しじゅう}{文句|もんく}を{言|い}っている。
{始終|しじゅう}を{話|はな}してください。
examples.english: Please tell me the whole story.
examples.notes: Noun usage: 始終 = the whole sequence of events

examples.japanese: この{問題|もんだい}については{始終|しじゅう}{考|かんが}えている。
examples.english: I'm constantly thinking about this problem.

examples.japanese: {事件|じけん}の{始終|しじゅう}を{警察|けいさつ}に{説明|せつめい}した。
examples.english: I explained the whole sequence of events to the police.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{事故|じこ}の{始終|しじゅう}を{目撃|もくげき}しており、{詳|くわ}しい{状況|じょうきょう}を{語|かた}ってくれた。
examples.english: She witnessed the entire incident and told us the detailed circumstances.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{始終|しじゅう}を{記録|きろく}に{残|のこ}した。
examples.english: I kept a record of the meeting from start to finish.

notes:
TWO USAGES:
1. Adverb: constantly, always
2. Noun: the whole story/sequence ({始終|しじゅう}を{話|はな}す = to tell the whole story)

SIMILAR WORDS (adverb meaning):
・いつも - always (most common, neutral)
・{常|つね}に - always (more formal)
・{絶|た}えず - incessantly, constantly
・しょっちゅう - frequently (casual)

{始終|しじゅう} often has a slightly negative nuance, suggesting something happens too much or annoyingly often.

[Register: Neutral to Slightly Formal]
